summary.text: A 37-year-old pregnant woman (gravida 3, para 2) with two previous cesarean deliveries was referred to a tertiary hospital with crampy abdominal pain of 16 h duration, vomiting that became bilious and progressive abdominal distension. She denied vaginal bleeding or trauma. On presentation she appeared acutely ill and in severe pain, with diffuse tenderness, rigidity and guarding and generalized peritonitis.

Vital signs and laboratory values were recorded. Bedside ultrasonography was unavailable and imaging was deferred because of generalized peritonitis. Surgical and obstetric teams jointly evaluated her, suspecting peritonitis from gangrenous bowel. Intravenous fluids, a nasogastric tube and ceftriaxone with metronidazole were started, and after discussion and consent she was taken for emergency laparotomy.

At laparotomy about 500 ml of hemorrhagic fluid was found, with approximately 20 cm of gangrenous small bowel twisted 360° around a cystic right adnexal mass that had undergone 720° torsion, with a gangrenous right ovary and fallopian tube. She underwent ileal resection with end-to-end anastomosis and right adnexectomy, and histopathology confirmed mature cystic teratoma.

She was monitored 36 h in the post-anesthesia care and recovery areas, recovered well on the ward over five days, and was discharged with follow-up. She had no new complaints at two, four and six weeks and returned to routine antenatal care. A repeat cesarean section at 38 weeks +2 days delivered a healthy 3.5 kg female neonate without complications, with normal follow-up visits afterwards.
